title: Aria’s Last Battle
dek: An uncertain expedition becomes a clash with Talan. Aria falls, Death kills the Zarathian troops, and the survivors fight over her body and Magnus’s life before escaping the Wyrm.

body:
Aria’s last battle began as a decision about where to send an army. Míriel’s interplanar scouts had found three possible fronts. The adventurers and Zarathian legions would have to choose one without knowing exactly what waited there.

What followed cost Zarathis its great cultural and military leader and the army that had marched with her. It also left the survivors arguing over whom they had come to protect, whether a fallen enemy deserved burial, and whether Magnus still belonged among them. The confrontation with Talan ended Aria’s life; the confrontation with Death nearly broke the company that survived her.

Choosing a war

Míriel’s scouts returned exhausted. One island lay in perpetual dusk, another was collapsing into ash, and the third still showed marble roads, towers and songs—until the apparent life flickered out of view. They could not be certain which island held the present battle. Aria would allow the adventurers to split if they wished, but refused to divide her legions.

The company did not agree about what the march should accomplish. Wren wanted to protect the innocent. Olokun wanted to draw the Zarathians away from a war that would strengthen Death. Scribonia argued that letting the army see the real conflict and suffer some losses might prevent greater destruction later. The prospect of fighting beside Aria had not made them trust her or one another.

Magnus favored the third island. Wren also thought the first two sounded like spent battlefields, and Eugene saw the possibility of making the third a forward position. Adelia’s divination gave both favorable and ominous signs. While the others were still struggling with their differences, Magnus called the choice to Aria. Míriel ordered the archmages to open the way. Wren sharply told Magnus that he had made the decision alone.

Through the Gates and into the storm

Aria, Arandiel and Míriel prepared the troops. Three Gates opened, and the legions marched to the third island. Its buildings were solid to the touch but strangely incomplete. Rooms stood empty; walls flickered; figures and laughter disappeared whenever the travelers tried to fix their attention on them. A smaller offshore island also seemed to come and go.

The army moved inland toward a great storm. Wren reached through the land with her magic and felt a clash larger than the island itself, as though worlds were colliding and the roots of Etz Chaim were in pain. She passed that warning to the others, then helped supply water for the march.

After hours at the army’s pace, Adelia began to tire. Jiangshi tried to support her and became exhausted too. The company still pressed on. At the storm’s edge, roughly nine hours after setting out, the troops halted. Magnus asked Aria about resting; Wren urged a pause so the soldiers would have strength left for the fight. They took a brief rest before entering.

Flying debris battered the company as they pushed toward the storm’s quieter center. The island’s apparent civilization gave way to ruins and signs of battle. At a huge pavilion they found a crater, a hole opening into nowhere and golden roots cut and shriveled at its edge. They had reached the front.

A battlefield with divided allegiances

Around the pit, divine warriors and angels fought Death Knights and Angels of Death. A wounded avatar stood among the gods’ forces. At their head was Talan. Aria saw him and called her soldiers forward for Zarathis.

The adventurers entered with different enemies in mind. Olokun concentrated on a Death Knight. Wren struggled to tell which combatants her companions intended to attack and asked whether the goal was to kill them all. Scribonia answered that they were fighting over the realm’s fate, but did not give her a clear answer about targets.

Scribonia called down a Meteor Swarm across the battlefield. Most of the remaining Heavenly Host fell to it. Talan sounded a horn for reinforcements and kept fighting. The god’s blows had already carried him through a long, bloody defense. Even wounded, he was still holding Death’s army back.

The company had reached a war in progress and changed its balance. Then the ground shook. Behind them, reality began to fade as something approached. They were running out of time even before Aria closed with Talan.

Talan and Aria

Aria met Talan’s raised weapon with her hand and held his gaze. Her hatred was unmistakable. It carried a long history of unanswered prayers and the divine authority she believed had failed her. Talan told her she was no god. Around them, the other fighting continued: Olokun finished a Death Knight, while the Zarathian troops tried to reach their leader.

At first Olokun could not believe she had misjudged the battle. He looked for the plan behind her confidence. The exchange became harder to deny. Talan was stronger. When he struck the mortals around her, Olokun shouted for him to stop and then turned against him. The Radiant Flame’s soldiers pressed toward the avatar, trying to save Aria.

Talan drove her to her knees. She lay bleeding and crushed beneath him. His declaration that Justice and Law were his very being was his own assertion in the fight. Scribonia, who hated Aria for what she had done to him, concealed a spell and struck at both her and Talan. Olokun’s grief and Scribonia’s desire for her death existed on the same battlefield.

Talan killed Aria. At his feet, Pride looked like a frightened girl who had tried to kill her monster. Talan took a moment of victory, then jumped into the opening in the Void. The remaining opposition was soon overcome. Aria did not rise, and her army had not reached her in time.

Death among the survivors

The rumbling grew louder. The Wyrm was coming. Death stepped out of the shadows, lamented Aria as his favorite and promised that Talan would pay. Then he flicked his hands and killed the Zarathian troops. He called them useless without her. The massacre followed her fall; these soldiers were not all casualties of Talan’s final blow.

Magnus dropped to his knees at the sight of his people and vomited. The surviving adventurers stood in a place where Death’s presence suppressed their magic. Eugene asked why he had killed people who were only misguided. Olokun moved to defend Aria’s body.

Death said he already possessed one of their companions, and Magnus collapsed. Eugene tried to heal him with the scroll Adelia had given him. Wren then loosed an arrow into Magnus, saying that giving him the benefit of the doubt had been a mistake. He later woke in blood and vomit and tried to get away from her.

Scribonia denied that Magnus was one of theirs. Olokun angrily opposed abandoning or killing the misguided, insisting that protection was still their purpose. Wren answered that Aria and Magnus had made choices while others had suffered in servitude. Their disagreement was about actual lives in front of them, and none of them could settle it by pointing to the enemy they had just defeated.

The body and the departure

Death wanted Aria’s body. He called her a faithful servant and his daughter, said he was proud of her, and said she had failed. Olokun stood in his way. Aria belonged to the people of Zarathis, he argued; Death had used her and had no right to call himself her father. These were competing claims over a person whose body still lay between them.

Scribonia urged Olokun to leave it, while Eugene stood beside him. Wren warned that Aria’s body was not worth another companion’s life. Jiangshi asked about burial among her ancestors. Death threatened the survivors with what might happen the next time one of their own died, then abandoned them to the approaching Wyrm.

As he left, suppressed magic returned. Scribonia recovered the relic Aria had carried. It was still on her; she had not had time to use it.

Olokun put Aria’s body into a bag of holding to bring it home for a funeral. Eugene had also moved to help recover it, then yielded that task. Scribonia called everyone to him, including Magnus. Magnus demanded a promise that neither Scribonia nor Wren would kill him. Scribonia promised for himself and credited Olokun’s words. They gathered while the Wyrm descended, and Scribonia’s Plane Shift carried them away.

A refuge without agreement

The escape worked. In the refuge beyond the battlefield, Magnus put out his mother’s cabin and asked to rest. Sleep did not come easily: the slaughter of his people replayed in his mind. He believed his soul was still Death’s, because his magic had returned when Death left. That remained Magnus’s explanation of his condition.

Olokun looked back on the risks he had taken arguing over Aria’s body. He had opposed her and still mourned her. Eugene sat apart, wondering what Death’s threat might cost the next companion to die. Wren looked at the body they had fought to recover and remembered the mass of dead soldiers left behind. The company had escaped together, but they had not reached a shared judgment of the battle.

Jiangshi played for the dead and tried to give Magnus some comfort. Scribonia wanted time to think before their next move. A rescued body, a recovered relic and living companions were what they could bring away. They could not bring the Zarathian army with them.

What her death leaves behind

Aria’s death removed an extraordinary cultural and military leader from Zarathis. The civic offices beside which she had acted did not disappear with her. The surviving company would still have to return her body, explain the expedition and face a people whose soldiers had been killed after their leader fell.

Later mourning and arguments about Aria carried both the lives she had harmed and the people who had loved her. Olokun’s wish to give her a funeral did not erase Scribonia’s captivity; Scribonia’s hatred did not erase her place in Zarathian life. Death’s power over Magnus in this scene did not establish that every previous choice Magnus made had been commanded by him.

Much later in Babel, Dumuzi claimed Aria was not dead. That later statement remains testimony. It does not undo the witnessed killing by Talan, identify a resurrection, or supply the missing history between this battlefield and his claim.

People and places in this history Aria / Pride · Magnus Niriin · Olokun · Scribonia · Wren · Eugene · Zarathis · authority after Aria
